Date of Notice: 2026-08-04
Requested Service: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
Treating Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 23472 (total shoulder arthroplasty), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-04. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in that notice, which gives a deadline of 2027-01-31.

1. Policy Under Which This Claim Was Reviewed

I understand from UnitedHealthcare's published medical policy, "Surgery of the Shoulder" (UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange Medical Policy, Policy Number 2026T0556GG), that CPT 23472 is addressed directly. That policy states:

"Surgery of the shoulder is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances. For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the: InterQual® CP: Procedures: o Arthroscopy or Arthroscopically Assisted Surgery, Shoulder o Arthroscopy or Arthroscopically Assisted Surgery, Shoulder (Adolescent) o Joint Replacement, Shoulder o Removal and Replacement or Revision, Joint Replacement, Shoulder. Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

I have not been able to obtain or review the underlying InterQual® CP "Joint Replacement, Shoulder" criteria referenced in this policy, because that content is a licensed, proprietary tool that is not published for member or public access. I am therefore not able to quote the specific data elements InterQual requires, and I am not attempting to do so. I respectfully request that UnitedHealthcare provide me and my surgeon's office with a copy of the specific InterQual criteria (and any internal checklist derived from it) that was applied to this request, so that we can confirm every required element has now been addressed. If a different or more specific medical policy or clinical guideline was actually used to make this determination, I request that it be identified and provided as well, consistent with the plan's obligation to disclose the specific internal rule or guideline relied upon in a denial.

2. The Denial Reason Was "Incomplete Documentation" — The Following Records Address That Gap

Because the denial was not based on a finding that my condition fails to meet medical necessity, but rather on a finding that the submitted file was incomplete, I am using this appeal to submit the full clinical record compiled by Dr. Marchetti's office. In the absence of the specific InterQual data elements (which have not been disclosed to me), I am organizing this record around the categories that are typically relevant to a shoulder joint replacement request — symptom duration and severity, conservative treatment history, imaging findings, and functional/exam findings — so the reviewer can identify precisely which, if any, element is still considered missing.

- Symptom duration and severity: I have had 9 months of progressive shoulder pain that is unrelieved by rest.

- Conservative treatment attempted and failed:
  • Supervised physical therapy focused on range-of-motion and periscapular strengthening: 10 weeks, from 2026-03-30 to 2026-06-08, with 18 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note (enclosed).
  • NSAID therapy for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
  • Corticosteroid injection administered 2026-03-30, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief.

- Imaging findings: Shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary views) dated 2026-05-23 show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. A CT scan confirms an intact rotator cuff.

- Functional limitation: I am unable to reach overhead, dress myself without help, or sleep on the affected side.

- Physical exam findings: Glenohumeral crepitus is present. Active forward elevation is limited to 90 degrees and external rotation to 10 degrees, with cuff strength intact on exam.

- No contraindications identified: No active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, BMI 29, non-smoker.

Copies of the physical therapy discharge note, injection administration record, radiology report and images dated 2026-05-23, CT report, and Dr. Marchetti's clinic notes documenting the exam findings and functional limitations above are enclosed with this appeal. [Insert list of specific enclosures/exhibit letters if the packet is paginated.]

3. Request

I ask that UnitedHealthcare:
(a) Reconsider the denial of CPT 23472 in light of the enclosed complete clinical record;
(b) Identify, in writing, the specific criterion or data element that was found to be missing from the original submission, if the file is still considered incomplete after this submission; and
(c) Provide the specific InterQual® CP "Joint Replacement, Shoulder" criteria (or any other internal guideline actually applied) that governs this determination, so that my surgeon and I can respond to it directly.

I further request that my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, be permitted a peer-to-peer conversation with the reviewing medical director if that would assist in resolving this appeal before the 180-day deadline of 2027-01-31.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address and phone number above, with a copy to Dr. Marchetti's office at [surgeon's office fax/phone/address].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,
